rounds.text: Xtranet Technologies Ltd is demonstrating exceptional fundamental momentum, highlighted by a compounded sales growth of 32% over the trailing twelve months and compounded profit growth of 35% over the same period [E15, E17]. Operational profitability is accelerating rapidly, with operating margin reaching 20% in September 2026 compared to 12% in the year-ago quarter, alongside a stellar return on equity of 34.8% [E13, E21]. Revenue visibility is robustly supported by an outstanding order book of INR 3,900 million as of September 30, 2026, complemented by a massive bid pipeline exceeding INR 2,000 crores [E73, E74]. Furthermore, the company's rules-based screen scores a high-confidence 93 out of 100, and a reverse DCF indicates that today's price implies an earnings growth of only 15.3%, which sits comfortably below the company's historical and projected performance [E37, E50]. Management's growth ambition is aggressive yet grounded in strategic execution, targeting revenue of over Rs. 500 crores for FY27—representing 35% to 40% growth—while capitalizing on the structural shift toward private enterprises and BFSI institutions [E62, E75]. Conceded: [E26] free cash flow was negative at Rs -22 Cr in March 2026 due to temporary working capital requirements for hardware and software procurement [E26, E76].

Xtranet Technologies is currently priced at a significant premium, trading at a P/E of 27.09x compared to a sector benchmark of 20.05x [E6] and a P/B of 4.51x against a benchmark of 1.94x [E7]. This valuation is particularly concerning given the company’s negative free cash flow of Rs -22 Cr in March 2026 [E26] and the fact that it pays no dividends to shareholders [E4, E49]. While the company claims to be growing, it faces substantial operational hurdles, including a 3x to 4x increase in hardware costs over the last year and ongoing challenges in product procurement [E77, E78]. These pressures have already forced a temporary increase in working capital requirements [E76], which, combined with high annualised volatility of 83.1% [E43], suggests a risky profile for investors. Furthermore, the stock is currently trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong historical ROE and ROCE metrics [E12, E13, E47] and maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.20x [E27].

The bear highlights a premium P/E of 27.09x and P/B of 4.51x [E6, E7], but ignores that these multiples are entirely justified by superior elite-tier returns, featuring a ROCE of 32.8% [E12] and an ROE of 34.8% [E13] that dwarf sector benchmarks [E8, E10]. Conceded: the company pays no dividend [E4, E49] and registered negative free cash flow of Rs -22 Cr in March 2026 [E26], but this cash burn is a deliberate and productive investment in working capital to support massive scaling [E76], backed by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.20x [E27]. The procurement challenges and hardware cost surges noted by the bear [E77, E78] have not derailed execution, as evidenced by a phenomenal 63% YoY revenue surge and 144% operational EBITDA growth in Q2 FY27 [E69], alongside a bulging order book of Rs 390 crores [E72]. The bear's reliance on technical moving averages [E40] ignores a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E41], and while annualised volatility is high [E43], it is paired with an exceptional Sharpe ratio of 3.28 [E44] and a robust rules-based screen score of 93 out of 100 [E50].

Conceded: the company displays a high relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E41], an exceptional Sharpe ratio of 3.28 [E44], and a rules-based screen score of 93 out of 100 [E50]. However, the bull's dismissal of valuation concerns by citing superior returns ignores that Xtranet's P/E of 27.09x and P/B of 4.51x still command significant premiums over sector benchmarks of 20.05x and 1.94x respectively [E6, E7], alongside a steep EV/EBITDA of 16.6x against a sector benchmark of 11.04x [E11]. Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio sits at a conservative 0.20x [E27], but framing negative free cash flow of Rs -22 Cr in March 2026 [E26] and a moderate cash conversion of 0.68x [E24] as a purely productive investment masks severe cash generation risks that are exacerbated by hardware costs surging 3x to 4x and severe procurement challenges [E77, E78]. Furthermore, the bull's reliance on recent top-line momentum glosses over the fact that the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are explicitly flagged as inconsistent [E22, E23], and that the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40] with an annualized volatility of 83.1% [E43].

Conceded: Xtranet's P/E of 27.09x, P/B of 4.51x, and EV/EBITDA of 16.6x sit above sector benchmarks [E6, E7, E11], but these premiums are fully justified by superior fundamentals like an ROE of 34.8% and ROCE of 32.8% [E13, E12]. Conceded: the yearly and quarterly operating margin trends are flagged as inconsistent [E22, E23], yet actual operating margins have structurally expanded by 11 percentage points to 17% annually and 20% quarterly [E20, E21], backed by surging H1 FY27 operational EBITDA growth of 123% [E70]. Conceded: free cash flow was negative at Rs -22 Cr in March 2026 [E26] alongside 83.1% volatility and positions below the 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40, E43], but this temporary working capital absorption directly supports a massive outstanding order book of Rs 3,900 million and a bid pipeline exceeding Rs 2,000 crores [E73, E74]. Rather than signaling fundamental weakness, the procurement of hardware enables the company to capture massive secular demand in data center infrastructure where capacity is slated to grow nearly fivefold by March 2030 [E63].

Conceded: ROE of 34.8% and ROCE of 32.8% [E12, E13]. However, those superior returns coexist with a premium P/E of 27.09x and P/B of 4.51x that outpace sector benchmarks [E6, E7], while delivering a 0.00% dividend yield to shareholders [E4]. Conceded: operational margins expanded and H1 FY27 operational EBITDA grew [E20, E21, E70], but filed statements explicitly flag the yearly and quarterly operating margin trends as inconsistent [E22, E23]. The bull claims negative free cash flow of Rs -22 Cr [E26] is merely temporary working capital absorption [E76], yet management simultaneously notes that hardware costs have surged 3x to 4x and procurement has become challenging [E77, E78]. Finally, while the order book and pipeline look large [E73, E74], high volatility of 83.1% and a price sitting below both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40, E43] demonstrate severe momentum risks that high return metrics alone cannot neutralize.

evidence.fact: The company is targeting revenue of over Rs. 500 crores for FY27, representing a growth of approximately 35% to 40%.
evidence.quote: Yes, so here targeting the FY26, we closed at Rs. 365 crore and we are targeting 500 plus crores for FY27. Approximately 35 to 40% of the growth.

evidence.fact: India's installed data center capacity is expected to increase nearly fivefold to approximately 7.5 gigawatts by March 2030.
evidence.quote: India's installed data center capacity is expected to increase nearly fivefold to approximately 7.5 gigawatts by March 2030, supported by the investment of more than INR 3 lakh crores over the next four, five financial years.

evidence.fact: Revenue growth for Indian IT service companies is projected at 3% to 5% in FY’27.
evidence.quote: Revenue growth for Indian IT service companies is projected at 3% to 5% in FY’27.

evidence.quote: Growth is driven by new data centre mandates and expanding managed services within existing accounts.

evidence.fact: The company formed a dedicated subsidiary focused on developing and operating data center infrastructure.
evidence.quote: An important strategic development during the quarter was the formation of Xtranet Data Center, a dedicated subsidiary focused on developing and operating data center infrastructure.

evidence.fact: Initially, the company is planning to start a 2MW data center with an expansion capacity of around 10MW.
evidence.quote: We have created a subsidiary because it is an asset-intensive business and initially we are planning to start with the 2MW with the expansion capacity of around 10MW.

evidence.fact: Putting up the initial 2MW data center will require roughly around Rs. 130 crores to Rs. 140 crores of investment.
evidence.quote: Chetan Anand: Sir, initially we are looking for putting up a 2MW data center which will be needing roughly around Rs. 130 crores, Rs. 140 crores of investment which will come partly from our internal accruals and partly from the money which will be raised through debt also.

evidence.quote: During Q2 FY’27, our consolidated revenue increased by 63% year-on-year to approximately Rs. 110 crores, while operational EBITDA grew by 144% to approximately Rs. 22 crores, with margins improving to 20.42%.

evidence.fact: For H1 FY’27, revenue grew by 42% to approximately Rs. 160 crores and operational EBITDA increased by 123% to approximately Rs. 33 crores.
evidence.quote: For H1 FY’27, revenue grew by 42% to approximately Rs. 160 crores. Operational EBITDA increased by 123% to approximately Rs. 33 crores, with EBITDA margins improving by 749 basis points to 20.49%.

evidence.fact: Operational EBITDA margins reached 20.42% in Q2 FY27, improving by 677 basis points year-on-year.
evidence.quote: Operational EBIDTA Margins (%) 20.42% 13.65% 677 Bps

evidence.fact: During Q2 FY’27, the company secured fresh orders of approximately Rs. 90 crores.
evidence.quote: During Q2 FY’27, we secured fresh order of approximately Rs. 90 crores, taking our order book to around Rs. 390 crores.

evidence.fact: The bid pipeline remained strong at over Rs. 2,000 crores.
evidence.quote: Our bid pipeline also remained strong at over Rs. 2,000 crores, providing opportunities to further expand our business.

evidence.fact: The company's outstanding order book stood at INR 3,900 million as of September 30, 2026.
evidence.quote: Outstanding order book of INR 3,900 Mn (as of September 30, 2026) across multiple states and clients provides revenue visibility and execution continuity over themediumterm.

evidence.fact: The government business contribution has now reduced to approximately 30% to 35%, marking a structural shift toward private enterprises and BFSI institutions.
evidence.quote: However, with increasing traction from private enterprises, BFSI institutions, and other corporate customers, our government business contribution has now reduced to approximately 30% to 35%.

evidence.fact: Securing timely availability of hardware and software and protecting margins against supply disruption temporarily increased working capital requirements.
evidence.quote: While this has temporarily increased our working capital requirements, we believe these investments will support stronger execution, revenue growth, and profitability during H2 FY’27.

evidence.fact: The cost of hardware has moved almost 3x to 4x in size over the last year.
evidence.quote: The cost of hardware has moved almost 3x-4x size basically.

evidence.fact: Procuring products has become a little bit of a challenge besides high prices.
evidence.quote: But till now, on our company side, we have not faced any kind of a cancellation or anything. We are very strategically working on wherein we can fulfil the requirement of the customer end-to-end and we are trying to cope up as of now.

evidence.quote: Sukhbir Singh Kukreja: The revenue contribution will start hopefully from the Q4 of this financial year.

evidence.fact: Management commitment: International expansion remains a strategic priority for exploring overseas business opportunities and technology partnerships.
evidence.quote: International expansion remains a strategic priority, with the company exploring overseas business opportunities, technology partnerships and collaborations to diversify its geographical revenue base.

evidence.quote: So, data center portion, we want to keep it at 50% of the overall revenue and year on year, we are expanding. We are looking forward to 35% to 40% of the annual growth in this segment from our business perspective.

evidence.quote: It will be close to 25 odd percent. That tax rate will be considered for the next two years, ma'am.
